page: Vultr vhp-1c-1gb-intel is an entry-level virtual server within the High Performance lineup, offering a single shared vCPU powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX-512 VNNI), and AES-NI hardware cryptography. Memory capacity is fixed at 1.0 GB of RAM. The instance includes 25 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, with zero dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest processing and throughput metrics characteristic of shared single-core hardware. Stress-ng single-core execution scored 1421.08, placing it in the average range, whereas overall multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics (1636.16) fell into the lowest decile due to the single-thread ceiling. Compression tasks showed stable capability, with single-threaded gzip achieving 23.84 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 8.95 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth measured 9.16 GB/sec for large un-cached reads and 7.89 GB/sec for writes. Workload benchmarks reflect the resource ceiling, delivering 1.58 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 1.37 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its shared CPU allocation and constrained 1.0 GB memory envelope, which limits concurrency and precludes memory-intensive runtimes. However, the integration of fast NVMe storage alongside modern vector instruction sets provides cost efficiency for low-tier operational tasks. Vultr vhp-1c-1gb-intel is technically configured for lightweight utility services, single-purpose microservices, development sandboxes, low-traffic web proxies, and basic background cron or automation jobs.
